s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive enlargement and discomfort of a digit with associated neurological symptoms and limited mobility
salient_findings: Enlargement of the left middle finger since birth
Limited flexion of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints
key_facts: The patient is a 14-year-old girl
The left middle finger has been larger than the others since birth
The finger has grown progressively over time
The patient developed tingling at the fingertip 3 months before presentation
There is limited flexion of the proximal and distal interphalangeal joints
The overlying skin of the enlarged finger is normal
There is tenderness throughout the enlargement
Sensation is decreased distally
Laboratory studies were unremarkable
A CT scan of the hand showed overgrowth of the phalanges and surrounding soft tissue

differentials: Giant cell tumor of the tendon sheath
per_call: Giant cell tumor of the tendon sheath

shortlist.label: Macrodactyly
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive enlargement of the finger since birth

shortlist.label: Lipofibromatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan showing overgrowth of phalanges and surrounding soft tissue

shortlist.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation to lipofibromatous hamartoma with soft tissue overgrowth

shortlist.label: Maffucci syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Enchondromas and soft tissue tumors can cause digit enlargement

shortlist.label: Ollier disease
shortlist.why_kept: Enchondromatosis can lead to progressive bone and soft tissue abnormalities

raw.rationale: The CT scan showing overgrowth of the phalanges and surrounding soft tissue, along with the clinical presentation of a progressively enlarging finger since birth and normal overlying skin, is consistent with fibrolipomatous hamartoma, a benign tumor composed of fibrofatty tissue.

rejected.label: Macrodactyly
rejected.why: While macrodactyly refers to an enlarged digit, it is more of a descriptive term rather than a specific diagnosis and does not account for the specific tissue characteristics seen on the CT scan.

rejected.label: Lipofibromatous hamartoma
rejected.why: This condition is less commonly described and the provided information does not specifically differentiate it from fibrolipomatous hamartoma in a way that would make it a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Maffucci syndrome
rejected.why: Maffucci syndrome involves multiple enchondromas and hemangiomas, which were not indicated in the CT scan or clinical presentation.

rejected.label: Ollier disease
rejected.why: Ollier disease is characterized by multiple enchondromas, which were not mentioned in the CT scan results or the clinical presentation.
